source: Refreshed by daily scheduled task. Sourced from Netflix Tudum, Tom's Guide, Apple TV Press, Amazon MGM Studios press, Crunchyroll Spring 2026 simulcast, Rotten Tomatoes critics picks. Skips already-watched titles in watched.json and titles in not-interested.json. Loved-list cross-check + watchlist availability check both ran 2026-04-29. Hero is Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle (Tier 1 Loved continuation + Tier 2 watchlist now-streaming). New 4/29 verifications: Widow's Bay sits at 100% Certified Fresh on RT after premiere reviews; Rick and Morty S9 Adult Swim premiere confirmed May 24 (US streaming on Hulu/Max Aug 31) — added as upcoming alert.

hero.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle
hero.about: First film in the trilogy adapting the Infinity Castle arc — the climactic showdown between the Demon Slayer Corps and Muzan's Upper Moons inside the shape-shifting fortress. Picks up directly from Hashira Training Arc. Made nearly $700M theatrically; Crunchyroll exec held it back from streaming until April 9, 2026 to protect the box office.
hero.why: Demon Slayer is on your Loved list — that's a higher-confidence signal than anything taste-extrapolated. Same studio (ufotable), same animation craft, an arc fans have been waiting years for. You pinned it; now it's actually on Crunchyroll. Tier 1 hero pick.

new_this_week.title: BEEF S2
new_this_week.about: Lee Sung Jin's Emmy-sweeping anthology resets with a brand-new cast and story: Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton, Cailee Spaeny. Two couples at a Montecito beach club — the younger pair blackmails the older pair after catching them on video in a violent fight. Eight ~30-min episodes dropped at once. 86% RT and currently #2 on Netflix's global top 10.
new_this_week.why: S1 was praised for exactly the things you reward — dark humor, plot escalation, ensemble acting — and the anthology reset means no S1 baggage.

new_this_week.title: Apex
new_this_week.about: Charlize Theron plays Sasha, an experienced climber grieving the loss of her partner; alone in the Australian wilderness, what begins as endurance becomes a cat-and-mouse hunt with a methodical predator (Taron Egerton). Directed by Baltasar Kormákur. Eric Bana co-stars.
new_this_week.why: Pure survival thriller — strong premise but no off-beat humor or sci-fi/supernatural angle to push it past 'try.' Good if you specifically want a tense one-night watch.

new_this_week.title: The Four Seasons S2
new_this_week.about: Comedy-drama from Tina Fey, Lang Fisher, Tracey Wigfield. Three couples reunite for seasonal getaways. Ensemble led by Fey, Steve Carell, Will Forte, Colman Domingo. Tone: middle-aged friendship dynamics, sharp dialogue, brisk runtime.
new_this_week.why: Witty banter + ensemble cast hits two of your signals. Lower-stakes than your usual sweet spot, but Fey's writing room is reliable for one-and-done evening watches.

new_this_week.title: Lord of the Flies
new_this_week.about: BBC miniseries adaptation of William Golding's novel — boys stranded on an island, society breaks down. Faithful take with prestige-drama production.
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation is a positive signal for you; psychological pressure-cooker setup has plot-twist potential. Tonally darker than your usual — try one episode.

new_this_week.title: Widow's Bay
new_this_week.about: Matthew Rhys plays the mayor of Widow's Bay, a sleepy fictional New England island town that may or may not be cursed. Created by Katie Dippold (writer of The Heat and Spy, alum of Parks & Rec). Eight-episode first season — two episodes today, then weekly through June 17. Currently 100% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes after premiere reviews; described by Rolling Stone as 'the best Stephen King mixtape ever.'
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist and just dropped today with a 100% RT debut. Off-beat tone, supernatural premise, ensemble acting, plot-twist machinery. Dippold also wrote two of your 'Loved' list films (The Heat, Spy). Highest-priority try this week.

new_this_week.title: Your Friends & Neighbors S2
new_this_week.about: Jon Hamm returns as Coop, the financial-titan-turned-suburban-burglar. James Marsden joins this season and reviewers single him out as scene-stealing. Apple's #1 show globally on launch week. Glossy crime caper with ensemble dialogue, escalating consequences, dark comic streak.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Strong critical reception, Hamm's best post-Mad Men work. Crime-comedy with witty banter and plot escalation is squarely in your strike zone.

new_this_week.title: Criminal Record S2
new_this_week.about: Peter Capaldi and Cush Jumbo return. After a young man is stabbed at a political rally, rival London detectives are forced into an uneasy alliance — what starts as a murder hunt escalates into an undercover operation against a far-right bomb plot. Eight episodes, one a week through June 10. 100% RT (5 reviews) — higher than S1's already 'certified fresh' 90%.
new_this_week.why: British police thriller with ensemble heavyweights, razor-sharp writing, escalating-plot machinery. Adjacent to the Slow Horses lane you 4⭐'d. Best critic-validated drop on Apple this month.

new_this_week.title: Outcome
new_this_week.about: Jonah Hill writes/directs. Keanu Reeves as a movie star blackmailed with footage from his past. Cameron Diaz, Matt Bomer, Jonah Hill co-star. 30% on Rotten Tomatoes — critics call it 'whiny, woe-is-me' with Hill stepping on his own ideas.
new_this_week.why: Cast looks promising on paper, but the reviews say Hill's directorial voice undercuts everything. Reviewers describe exactly the 'overly artsy without paying off' miss-pattern you've flagged. Skip unless you're a Reeves completionist.

new_this_week.title: The Boys S5 (Final)
new_this_week.about: Fifth and final season. Two-episode premiere April 8, weekly thereafter, finale May 20. The world is firmly under Homelander's control; the remaining Boys are scattered. Jensen Ackles back as Soldier Boy.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Final season of a satirical superhero show with the dark-humor + off-beat + supernatural triad you reward. Currently airing weekly — good time to start catching up.

new_this_week.title: Kevin
new_this_week.about: Animated comedy from Aubrey Plaza, Jason Schwartzman, Amy Sedaris, Whoopi Goldberg. A lifelong housecat decides he no longer wants to live with people. Tone: absurd, character-driven adult animation.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Aubrey Plaza voice work + absurd premise + 30-min runtime is a clean fit for your bedtime-watch habit.

new_this_week.title: The House of the Spirits
new_this_week.about: Eight-episode prestige adaptation of Isabel Allende's novel spanning nearly half a century of one Chilean family. Told in Spanish, cast drawn from across Latin America and Spain. Variety calls it sumptuous and rewarding; some critics flag it as bland in execution.
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation, magical-realism, Spanish-language all positive signals — but reviews lean toward 'sad family epic,' which is your lower-priority lane. Try one episode; if it's leaning more drama than fantasy, bail.

new_this_week.title: Spider-Noir
new_this_week.about: Live-action Marvel series. Nicolas Cage plays an aging private investigator in 1930s New York who's also the only Spider-Man in his black-and-white universe. Tonally: pulp noir, period detective drama with superhero elements.
new_this_week.why: Off-beat premise + period-noir framing + Cage-doing-Cage is the exact weirdness you tend to enjoy. Genre crossover (superhero + noir) keeps it from being a typical cape show.

new_this_week.title: Witch Hat Atelier
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited adaptation of Kamome Shirahama's award-winning manga. A young girl named Coco, who isn't supposed to be able to do magic, accidentally casts a spell and is taken on as an apprentice by a wandering witch. Studio BUG FILMS. Critics calling the premiere one of 2026's best anime episodes.
new_this_week.why: World-building is one of your strongest signals; reviewers highlight 'warmth and melancholy' over Dorohedoro's edge. If Frieren's tone landed for the genre, this is the same lane done very well.

new_this_week.title: Dorohedoro S2
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited return after six years. Lizard-headed Caiman tries to find the magic-user who transformed his head — while teaming up with his friend Nikaido. Tone: dark, surreal, gory, and somehow heartfelt. 11 episodes. MAPPA animation.
new_this_week.why: Off-beat + supernatural + dark humor is your sweet spot. Critics call it 'singular,' fans 9–10/10 the return. If you wanted Demon Slayer's kinetic energy with weirder flavor, here it is.

new_this_week.title: Liar Game
new_this_week.about: From Madhouse (Death Note, Monster). A woman gets sucked into a brutal underground game where 100 million yen is at stake — players use deception and persuasion to bankrupt each other. Episodic mind-game structure with a connecting arc.
new_this_week.why: Plot-twist appetite + dark psychology + Madhouse pedigree. Reviews call early episodes a bit talky but say the mind-games escalate well. Lower-stakes try than Dorohedoro.

new_this_week.title: Chainsaw Man — The Movie: Reze Arc
new_this_week.about: Theatrical-to-streaming release of the Chainsaw Man arc adapting manga chapters 39-52. A heartbreaking romance against an action backdrop with Devils. Reviewers describe sequences as 'best action scenes in recent memory.' Grossed over $160M globally; debuts on Crunchyroll Apr 30 in both subbed and dubbed, kicking off Crunchyroll's Ani-May celebration.
new_this_week.why: Supernatural + action + tight 1h40 runtime is bedtime-friendly. If you don't already know Chainsaw Man S1, the Reze Arc still works as a relatively standalone film entry. Perfect Friday-night option.

critics.title: Criminal Record S2
critics.about: Peter Capaldi and Cush Jumbo return. London-set police thriller — what starts as a murder hunt at a political rally escalates into an undercover op against a far-right bomb plot. 100% on Rotten Tomatoes (5 reviews).
critics.why: Highest critic score on a platform you have this month. British police thriller adjacent to your Slow Horses lane. Most-watched on Apple TV+ globally one day after premiere.

critics.title: Widow's Bay
critics.about: Matthew Rhys, Stephen King-flavored New England horror-comedy from Katie Dippold (The Heat, Spy). 100% Certified Fresh on RT at premiere. Two episodes drop today, weekly through Jun 17.
critics.why: Bullseye fit — Dippold wrote two of your Loved-list films, supernatural + dark comedy is your sweet spot, and the critic consensus is the strongest of the week. Same pick as 'new this week' on purpose: when the watchlist title and the critic favorite collapse onto the same show, it's worth saying twice.

critics.title: How to Get to Heaven from Belfast
critics.about: Lisa McGee's (Derry Girls) follow-up. Three lifelong Belfast friends travel to Donegal when the estranged fourth member of their teenage friend group dies unexpectedly. What starts as paying respects becomes a chaotic quest to solve her death while keeping their own dark secret buried. Six-episode comedy mystery; 95% RT.
critics.why: Bullseye fit. McGee's Derry Girls-honed Irish/British humor + comedy-mystery format engineered for plot twists + ensemble of great character actors. Strong taste-match outside the hero pick.
